label: PBI report build
info: Builds Plan_OPT_EU, Time_Utilisation_EU and Daily_Losses_EU (the Tableau tables) from the Provideam CSV files in the data lake, to <root>/report or <root>/candidate/provideam by the source of each line in Config. No API calls. Needs the Config tab.

name: [1] TRIGGER & TASK SETTINGS
info: STAGE 1 - TRIGGER AND TASK SETTINGS. Builds the three Tableau tables Plan_OPT_EU, Time_Utilisation_EU and Daily_Losses_EU from the Provideam CSV files in the data lake, one file per site and month, with Dept, Area and Product Type from the Machine Names file of the site, Data Source = Provideam and In EU Report from the report scope file (false: rows the EU pages leave out). The rows of a line whose source in 1.1 CONFIG is Provideam go to <root>/report (what Tableau reads), the rows of a line on another source to <root>/candidate/provideam. The inject payload is the job: {"tables": [...], "sites": [...], "from": "YYYY-MM", "to": "YYYY-MM"}; a missing list means all, missing months mean last month and this month. Nothing is written while the table is true in DRY_RUN of 1.1.

name: 1.0 Take queued job
1.1 TASK SETTINGS (edit here)
1.2 Start jobs
[2] SITE SETUP: GLIDEPATHS
info: STAGE 2 - one message per site (plan OPT, time utilisation and daily losses share this setup): the folder eu_report/reference/glidepaths/site=<Site>/ is listed, the newest .csv is read and parsed, and the target lookup of the site is stored in flow context: machine-site and month (01/MM/YYYY) give the OEE target (bucket "% OEE"), the PDT target ("Planned Downtime (Total)") and the UPDT target ("Unplanned Downtime (Total)"), as the three target queries of the report do after the unpivot. A site without a file stops here and the log says so.

name: 2.1 Set glidepaths folder
2.2 Pick the file
2.3 Build target lookup
[3] SITE SETUP: MACHINE NAMES
info: STAGE 3 - the Machine Names file of the site (<root>/reference/machine_names/site=<Site>/, newest .csv) is listed, read and parsed, and the lookup MachineName to Dept, Area and Product Type is stored in flow context, for every machine of the file (the EU scope is the column In EU Report, from the report scope file). A machine missing from the file has empty Dept, Area and Product Type. A site without a file stops here and the log says so.

name: 3.1 Set machine names folder
3.2 Pick the file
3.3 Build machine lookup
[4] SITE SETUP: SHIFT PATTERNS
info: STAGE 4 - the Shift Patterns file (eu_report/reference/shift_naming/site=All/) is listed, read and parsed, and the lookup raw shift name to Shift is stored in flow context (the report joins ShiftName to the Shift Type column and keeps the Shift; an unknown name gives an empty shift).

name: 4.1 Set shift folder
4.2 Pick the file
4.3 Build shift lookup
[5] SITE SETUP: REPORT SCOPE
info: STAGE 5 - the report scope file (<root>/reference/report_scope/site=All/, newest .csv, one row per rule: Site, Tables, Rule keep or drop, Column, Value) is listed, read and parsed, and the rules of the site are stored in flow context. They set the column In EU Report of every table (false: a row the EU pages leave out, the site pages keep). Then the site goes on to the tables of the job.

name: 5.1 Set report scope folder
5.2 Pick the file
5.3 Build scope lookup
5.4 Route the site
[6] PLAN OPT: MONTHS
info: STAGE 6 - the month files of the site (eu_report/pbi_report/source/plan_opt/site=<Site>/plan_opt_YYYY-MM.csv) are listed and the months of the job that exist are chosen (a missing month is logged and skipped: a read node would stop on a missing file). One message per month, one per second.

name: 6.1 Set plan OPT folder
6.2 Choose months
[7] PLAN OPT: ROWS
info: STAGE 7 - one month of one site: the file is read and parsed, then Plan_OPT_EU rows (only the machines both reports drop are left out, shift name from the Shift Patterns file, minutes without seconds, Unique Machine Name, Product Key, the three targets of the month) and Time_Utilisation_EU rows (sum per machine and day, minutes with seconds) are built. Out 3 is a check line: rows read, kept, left out, shifts without a mapping, machines without a target.

name: 7.1 Set month file
7.2 Build plan rows
[8] Plan_OPT_EU
info: STAGE 8 - Dept, Area, Product Type from the machine lookup of the site, Data Source = Provideam and In EU Report from the scope rules are added, the rows are split by the source of their line in 1.1 CONFIG (a line on Provideam: <root>/report, any other: <root>/candidate/provideam, one message per folder), then decide (nothing is written in dry-run mode or for an empty month), parquet, the month path <folder>/Plan_OPT_EU/site=<Site>/Plan_OPT_EU_<YYYY-MM>_provideam.parquet and write object. A rerun replaces the month.

name: 8.1 Add machine and scope columns
8.2 Split by source
8.3 Decide Plan_OPT_EU
8.4 Set Plan_OPT_EU month path
[9] Time_Utilisation_EU
info: STAGE 9 - the same for Time_Utilisation_EU: one row per machine and day, total, planned and OEE time summed in minutes, All Time 1440.

name: 9.1 Add machine and scope columns
9.2 Split by source
9.3 Decide Time_Utilisation_EU
9.4 Set Time_Utilisation_EU month path
[10] LOSSES: EQUIPMENT
info: STAGE 10 - daily losses only: the Equipment Coding file of the site (eu_report/reference/equipment_coding/site=<Site>/) is read and the lookup "machine + loss description" to equipment is stored in flow context (an empty equipment is "Unclassed", as in the report queries). Weinheim has no Merged Unique Identifier column: the key is built from machine and description.

name: 10.1 Set equipment folder
10.2 Pick the file
10.3 Build equipment lookup
[11] LOSSES: MONTHS
info: STAGE 11 - the month files of three types are listed for the site (volume loss correction, plan OPT, line losses) and the months that exist are stored (an optional type with a missing month is skipped, a read node would stop on it). The months of the job that have a line loss file are chosen: one message per month, one per second.

name: 11.1 Set correction folder
11.2 Store correction months
11.3 Set plan OPT folder
11.4 Store plan OPT months
11.5 Set line loss folder
11.6 Choose months
[12] LOSSES: CORRECTION
info: STAGE 12 - one month of one site: the volume loss correction file of the month (loss units and time per date, machine, group, subgroup and description, text replacements of the site as in the report) is read and a lookup is stored in flow context. A month without a file goes on with an empty lookup (no loss units).

name: 12.1 Set month
12.2 Set correction file
12.3 Build correction lookup
[13] LOSSES: VOLUME TOTALS
info: STAGE 13 - the plan OPT file of the month gives the volume total per machine and day (the sum of Capacity, the Targets Volume query of the report). A month without a plan file goes on with an empty lookup.

name: 13.1 Set plan OPT file
13.2 Build volume totals
[14] LOSSES: ROWS
info: STAGE 14 - the line loss file of the month is read and the rows are built with the steps of the report queries of the site (duplicate stops, group filter, the machines both reports drop, shift name, volume key and loss units from the correction, equipment, text replacements of the subgroup, loss target key and value from Glidepaths, volume total). Out 2 is a check line: rows read, kept, filtered, without loss units, equipment or target.

name: 14.1 Set line loss file
14.2 Build loss rows
[15] Daily_Losses_EU
info: STAGE 15 - the same for Daily_Losses_EU: machine columns, split by source, decide, parquet, the month path <folder>/Daily_Losses_EU/site=<Site>/Daily_Losses_EU_<YYYY-MM>_provideam.parquet and write object.

name: 15.1 Add machine and scope columns
15.2 Split by source
15.3 Decide Daily_Losses_EU
15.4 Set Daily_Losses_EU month path
[16] SITE SETUP: FAILED
info: STAGE 16 - a Glidepaths, Machine Names, Shift Patterns, report scope or Equipment Coding file that is missing or empty: one log line, nothing is built for that site.

name: 16.1 Describe failure
[17] ERRORS
info: STAGE 17 - a catch node takes every error raised by a node of this tab and turns it into a log line with the name of the node and the message of the API (for example the limit message of evaluateKPIs). Errors of the log nodes themselves are not logged again.

name: 17.1 Describe error
[18] LOG
info: STAGE 18 - every log line arrives here through the link "to LOG". 1 turns a line into a row (time, flow, site, production day, level) and shows it in the debug sidebar. The join collects the rows for 30 s, the delay lets one batch pass every 10 s so two writes do not overlap, 3 sets the file of the month and the read node loads the old file. A read of a file that does not exist answers nothing (only a warning), so the same batch also goes through a 10 s wait to the append step. The log is written whatever the dry-run switch says.

name: 18.1 Format log line
18.2 Note last log line
18.3 Build log write
[19] LOG WRITE
info: STAGE 19 - adds the rows of the batch to the old file and writes the whole file back (the data lake has no append). Columns: ts_utc, seq, flow, site, production_day, mode, level, source, message. Every field is quoted, line breaks become a space. The batch arrives twice (read answer and the wait) and is written once. If the read gives no answer for a file this flow wrote before, a new file with a time stamp is written, so the history is never replaced.

name: 19.1 Append log rows
